chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Faddal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'God has given the People of the Book a lot of good.' He said: 'And what is that?'

I said: 'The word of God the Exalted: [28:52] Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they are believers in it — up to His words: [28:54] Those shall be given their reward twice because they were patient.'
He (the narrator) said: Then he (the Imam) said: 'God has given you just as He gave them.' Then he recited:
[57:28] O you who believe! Fear God and believe in His Messenger: He will give you two portions of His mercy, and make for you a light by which you will walk.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book — Jews and Christians who received previous scriptures
key_terms.تَأْتَمُّونَ: You follow/take as Imam — from the same root as 'Imam', meaning to follow in leadership
key_terms.كِفْلَيْنِ: Two portions/shares — a double reward referenced in Quran 28:54 and 57:28
key_terms.نُوراً تَمْشُونَ بِهِ: A light by which you walk — interpreted by the Imam as the Imam himself, the divine guide

ai.seo_question: What does Quran 57:28 mean according to Imam al-Baqir, and how is the 'light' interpreted in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Abu al-Jaroud asked Imam al-Baqir (AS) about the great reward God promised the People of the Book who accepted the Prophet. The Imam asserted that God has given the believers an equivalent blessing, then recited Quran 57:28 and interpreted 'the light by which you walk' as the Imam whom the believers follow. This hadith is central to the chapter on the Imams as the light of God, presenting Quranic exegesis that identifies the Imam — not just the Prophet — as the divinely-given light and guide for the community.
